newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans collapse on stocks data, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans collapse on stocks data, technicals.

text.p: News USDA left its estimate for 1996-97 soybean ending stocks unchanged at 125 million bushels sent CBOT soybean futures spiralling lower on Monday and sparked a key technical reversal, traders said.

"There was a lot of speculative liquidation in beans. There was general disappointment over the failure of USDA to lower the stocks carryout," said Joel Karlin, senior grains analyst for Everen, Securities.

USDA on Monday put ending stocks at 125 million bushels, steady with its previous estimate. Also, USDA raised its crush figure by five million bushels but that was offset by an increase in its import estimate, sources said.

The USDA data pushed soybeans down only slightly on the open and the market turned higher in morning trade after USDA put weekly export sales above trade expectations. USDA said 12.536 million bushels were inspected for export, above trade estimates for six million to 10 million bushels.
Floor sources said locals were sellers near midday and stops were hit below $8.83 in the July, sending old crop months into a free-fall that ended in a key reversal.
Soybeans ended 20-1/2 to 3-1/2 cents a bushel lower with July down 20-1/2 at $8.68-1/2.
New crop November fell six cents to $7.04-1/2 a bushel.
"The weekly shipments were quite impressive, but we didn't make any new highs out of it," said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter.
Technical traders said the old crop contracts broke through support and fell sharply through several chart gaps. They pegged $8.53 as the next downward objective for the July.

"Bull markets need something new to keep them going, and there really wasn't anything new in the report," a floor trader said. "Once we got back below $8.82 in the July, we hit stops and it just fed off itself."
November escaped with only minor losses amid forecasts for a cool, wet week in the U.S. Midwest. That scenario suggested soybean plantings would slow.
On the day, E.D. and F. Man International sold two million bushels July, ING sold one million July and Refco Inc sold 2.5 million November, pit sources said.
Rosenthal Collins spread 2.2 million bushels November/July at $1.75-1/2 to $1.76, premium July.
In options trade, D.T. Trading sold 300 July $8.25 puts at 4-3/4 cents and Rosenthal Collins bought 300 July $9.00 calls at 27-1/2 to 27-3/4 cents.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 60,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 40,006.
